newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Possible U.N. candidate meets Indonesia's Suharto.
newsitem.headline: Possible U.N. candidate meets Indonesia's Suharto.

text.p: The head of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference met with President Suharto on Thursday to ask for Indonesia's support if he seeks the office of United Nations secretary-general.
Indonesia, the world's most populous Moslem country, made no comment on the possible candidacy of Hamid Algabid.
But Foreign Minister Ali Alatas later told reporters: "Indonesia can understand the desire of the African nations to fill the position of secretary-general."

Algabid, a former prime minister of Niger, has hinted he will seek the top U.N. job if Washington vetoes the reappointment of Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to a second term, as it has threatened to do.
Algabid has said he will not run against Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian whose first five-year term ends in December.
Some in Africa fear that if the United States blocks Boutros-Ghali, the continent will lose the second five-year term normally accorded to the secretary-general.
"I have been told by the president to look into the matter," Alatas said, adding that it was not certain that the United States would veto Boutros-Ghali's reappointment.
